messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, Sep 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: DPA redlines — archive/DR carveouts + subprocessor consent

Hi Dylan & Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. Our legal team flagged two areas we'd like to resolve before signature:

1) Backup/DR carveouts — we need explicit carveout language for our clinical records that are subject to state retention laws. Our counsel is asking for a narrow exception allowing Redwood to maintain encrypted backups for DR purposes for up to 5 years, provided data is isolated and not used for training.

2) Subprocessor consent flow — we need an explicit notification window (30 days) with right to object for critical subprocessor additions and a process for listing subprocessors (we prefer a registry URL).

I've attached our redlines (Sunrise_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf). Can we sync early this week to agree language? We prefer DocuSign for execution.

Best,

Laura Chen
Head of Legal Operations
Sunrise Health

Appreciate the clear flags. Quick takes:

- Backup/DR: We can accept a 5-year encrypted backup carveout limited to DR-only use, with explicit prohibition on training. We'll add language requiring customer-approved encryption keys or KMS binding.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessor register (public URL). We can implement a 30-day notice window for new critical subprocessors; if you object within 30 days we'll either remove the subprocessor or agree mitigations.

I'll loop in Legal Ops (Marissa) and our Security lead if we need to tighten KMS language. Can you do a 30-minute call tomorrow at 11am PT? If that works we'll confirm final redlines and send via DocuSign.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, Oct 01, 2026 at 2:22 PM PDT
Subject: Re: DPA redlines — archive/DR carveouts + subprocessor consent

Laura —

Thanks for the redlines. Following up with proposed clause drafts so we can move directly to DocuSign after the call:

1) Backup/DR carveout (proposed): "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, Customer agrees that Provider may retain encrypted backups containing Customer Data for disaster recovery purposes for a period not to exceed five (5) years. Such backups shall be used solely for disaster recovery and shall not be processed for model training or other analytics. Provider shall segregate Customer Data in backups and make commercially reasonable efforts to honor Customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) where contractually feasible."

2) Subprocessor notice (proposed): "Provider maintains a current list of subprocessors at [registry URL]. Provider will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of any new critical subprocessor. Customer may object in writing during the notice period; following an objection Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to address Customer concerns, which may include removing the subprocessor or implementing technical and contractual mitigations."

If those read OK we can finalize and send via DocuSign. Dylan — I penciled the 11am PT slot for tomorrow and added a brief agenda: (1) confirm KMS language, (2) confirm 'critical' subprocessor definition, (3) sign and return.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
